name: Dark Tan
lede: Dark Tan is a deeper, more golden [[tan]], classed by the ISCC-NBS system as a dark orange yellow, and one of the most common swatches in our whole archive.

sections.title: The name
sections.body:
No book in our library records a name at this position before the xkcd color survey of 2010, where the public supplied the plain descriptive phrase "dark tan" [1]. Its origin before that survey is undocumented here [1].

The nearest ISCC-NBS 1955 block is dark orange yellow, a little over 5 CIEDE2000 units away, with a Munsell reading near 0.7Y in hue [1]. The nearest named colors on file are [[pinchbeck-brown]], [[isabella-color]] and [[chamoline]], at 2.7, 2.8 and 3.5 ΔE [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds a match for this swatch in 2,713 of 23,781 paintings, or about 11 per cent, as photographed [2]. That makes it one of the more common named colors in the whole archive, present across centuries from the 1100s to the 1900s with no sharp peak [2]. Giovanni di Paolo and Maarten van Heemskerck both carry it at over five times the baseline rate, and it is common across Iran, India, Korea and Japan alike [2]. The words "Ochre" and "Camel" share its canvases more than chance, and it plays a highlight role in most of its paintings [2].
